subject: Linguistics
title: Irregular Forms
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Irregular Forms.

hook.text: 'Go' becomes 'went'—not 'goed.' Why doesn't English follow its own rules?

buildup.text: Irregular forms are survivors from older stages of the language that resisted regularization.

discovery.text: 'Went' actually comes from the old verb 'wenden,' which merged with 'go' centuries ago.

twist.text: Children say 'goed' and 'mouses' because their brains apply regular rules by default.

climax.text: High-frequency words resist regularization longest—you say 'is/are/was' daily, keeping them alive.

punchline.text: Irregular forms survive by being used too often to forget.

quiz.question: Why do children say 'goed' instead of 'went'?
options: They apply regular rules by default
